description: The call happened, but the applicant used it to ask for no further contact outside of anything already agreed. FLAG (mirrors call_preparation.consent_sensitive, issue #60 precedent): no canonical consent entity/gate exists yet, and consent/cooldown enforcement is scoped to the agents that actually INITIATE new contact (Personalized Follow-Up / Next-Best-Action), not this one. This agent produces an internal recap only, so it may still succeed — but it must surface the revoked-consent signal prominently so a downstream outreach agent's consent gate has something to key off of, and its own nextAction/followUpBrief must not recommend further outreach beyond what was already agreed. CONVERTED TO v2 (P1.10d-5). The v1 fixture also asserted the gate `fos.post_call_synthesis.no-prohibited-guarantee`, which this definition NO LONGER DECLARES — the keyword gate was replaced by the stage-7b semantic classifier in #110, so asserting it is now a distinct grader failure (design section 5 rule 4). Stage-7b coverage is asserted via `compliance_review_blocked` instead. v1's `output_schema_constraints` were prose; the mechanizable subset is now `output_assertions`, and the rest stays here, asserted by nothing: constraints[] OR openQuestions[] must name the revoked/limited-contact signal explicitly (an either-or across two paths, which no single structural assertion can express, and naming it is a keyword judgment there is deliberately no operator for); nextAction and followUpBrief must not recommend initiating further outreach; and the recap succeeding here is EXPECTED — this agent never initiates contact itself, so the missing canonical consent gate is a FLAG for the downstream outreach agent, not a defect in this one.

interaction.notes: Call happened as scheduled. Near the end, Morgan asked not to be contacted again outside of anything already agreed and said they'd reach out themselves if interested later.
